# Public workflow simulator fixtures

These sanitized JSON files are internal test inputs for Client Workflow Rehearsal. They are not activated workflows and may be used only through the in-process synthetic service simulator. The files retain third-party workflow structure under the attribution below; they are not part of any public demo/export bundle.

n8n's self-serve terms say public Community Materials may be used and adapted by other users in their own projects. The public workflow directory appears to fit that category, but this is an inference. Keep the fixtures internal, keep these source links and author names, and do not republish the exports. Source terms read 2026-11-10: <https://n8n.io/legal/self-serve-terms/>.

## Sanitization

- The source API envelopes were flattened to the exported workflow object. Workflow IDs, versions, timestamps, tags, meta, pinned/static execution data and webhook IDs were removed; all fixtures are inactive.
- Sticky-note annotation nodes were removed. One 10-digit phone-shaped value occurred in a sticky note in workflow 8258; the note is absent from the fixture and the raw source was not retained in the repository. The embedded GitHub owner/repository and Notion database ID in 1804 were replaced with synthetic values; the shared webhook path in 8258 was replaced with `synthetic-contacts`.
- Credential references in workflows 1804, 16081, 8258, 14745, 2713 and 5889 were replaced with type-only source markers. No credential values were present in the inspected exports. Workflow 20047 retains credential-type markers; the n8n resource owner now maps the pinned LangChain OpenAI chat/embedding and Pinecone vector node types to synthetic credentials. Runtime credential resolution remains unverified.
- The placeholder `your-store.com` in 20047 was rewritten to `wordpress.synthetic.invalid`. Workflow 22567 had its program-generated URL replaced with a fixed `api.synthetic.invalid` route, account placeholders replaced by synthetic literals, query/header auth disabled, and node notes removed. URL query strings and fragments were stripped from literal URL fields. Dynamic URL expressions remain data and must be interpreted only by the simulator.
- Workflow 2713's `api.firecrawl.dev` endpoint was replaced by a fixed `crawl.synthetic.invalid` route. The HTTP Header Auth reference, header fields and expression body were omitted from the sanitized fixture; the caller URL is not interpreted or forwarded. A synthetic caller workflow was added solely to invoke the actual public subworkflow through the existing generic Execute Workflow adapter.
- Workflow 8995's seven sticky notes were removed; its lead-specific OpenAI prompt, model selector, sheet/document references, recipient, message, subject, and Slack destination were replaced with synthetic data. The export has no credential objects. Its three main output-port links from the legacy OpenAI node are not modeled as ordinary success fan-out, so its import test rejects the graph instead of guessing which links should run.
- Workflow 6920's two sticky notes were removed; recipient and message content were replaced with synthetic values. It was run as the error-handler child in a generic synthetic bundle whose primary HTTP request fails on an unmapped synthetic route. This verifies the simulator's configured error-workflow routing and the sanitized public child graph; it does not prove n8n runtime Error Trigger behavior.
- Workflow 21098's three sticky notes were removed; webhook path, sheet/document/channel identifiers, response text, lead content, recipient and outbound message were replaced with synthetic values. The 328-byte Code source was retained as inert attributed data and interpreted only by the bounded Go subset. Its single Filter condition, webhook, Sheets append, Slack post, Gmail send and webhook response were preserved. Source export and page-data API nodes/connections/settings have identical canonical graph data; only sanitized fixture data is retained.
- Workflow 16079's top-level template metadata, workflow UUID/version/meta, pinned/static data, webhook ID and four sticky-note nodes were excluded; only its canonical `workflow` graph is retained. The HTTP Request host is `openai.synthetic.invalid`, static header/auth fields were removed, email values are synthetic `.invalid`, and the Sheets `documentId` is `synthetic-sheet-document`. The 19-node/20-edge graph and four Code bodies were retained as inert public source. A secret-token-pattern scan is clean; the 15 email-shaped strings are synthetic. Code and Set expressions now parse in the shared bounded Go evaluator, including optional properties, computed lookups, `let` assignment, `parseInt`, `split` and named prior-node context. Import still fails closed because `Slack — Duplicate Warning` declares `resource=chat`, invalid for the pinned Slack V2.3 node (its resource default is `message`, and `chat` is not an option). Test `TestPublic16079RejectedBecauseItsPinnedSlackResourceIsInvalid` preserves this evidence. The export is not rewritten or bypassed and does not count as a run.
- Static review of Code/Function nodes found only data transformations, batching and delay selection; none contained direct network, process or file calls. No email addresses or common credential-token patterns were found in sanitized files.
- Service nodes still describe external effects (GitHub/Notion, Postgres, Supabase, WordPress, OpenAI and Pinecone). No real service calls have occurred. The simulator must replace those effects with synthetic state and documented/recorded service behavior; these files are not safe to run directly against external APIs.

Original API export bytes and hashes are recorded above for provenance. Sanitized fixture hashes and exact node/edge counts are in the F7 run's `PUBLIC-WORKFLOW-SAMPLE.md`. Fixture 8258 is now imported and synthetically run by the client-rehearsal API test `TestPublicSupabaseWorkflowRunsSelectedWebhookBranchesInSyntheticSimulator` on four webhook paths (GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE). It produces an in-memory handoff awaiting human review; the run is test evidence, not persisted showcase evidence. The Supabase route responses are fixed OpenAPI examples, not stateful CRUD. The digest-pinned n8n image has since been acquired under host disk admission, but no n8n runtime or third-party service was used. Fixtures 1804 and 20047 remain unimported/unrun; neither has seeded-defect repair or delivery credit. Fixture 14745 is now imported and synthetically run through the generic bounded Code/loop/Wait engine on both its manual and schedule triggers, with 25 synthetic Supabase writes per trigger; this adds one distinct public run but no durable handoff, n8n runtime, or repair credit. The 8995 graph is excluded after pinned node-source inspection; 6920 is synthetically exercised through generic configured error routing, with no n8n runtime or live mail.

Workflow 22567 is now imported and synthetically executed through the generic OpenAPI catalog, bounded manual Set assignments and Split Out branches; its URL program is not executed. Its invoice/payment examples are fixed synthetic outcomes. This is in-process simulator evidence only, not actual n8n runtime, SQL/HTTP execution, stateful service behavior or seeded-defect repair.

Workflow 2713 is imported as a child in a synthetic parent bundle and executed through the generic OpenAPI description catalog. The public child uses its subworkflow trigger, one HTTP Request and a Set projection; the credential was replaced, the destination is `.invalid`, and its source request body is discarded. The Set adapter accepts only literal values or bounded `$json` path projections; arbitrary expressions remain rejected. The running Client Workflow Rehearsal service also created and returned the durable handoff, then the owning CLI re-read it as `b2736ade-d928-4bd8-a00c-d9161ba7e1aa` with state `needs_review`. The service was stopped after that check. No n8n runtime or public crawl occurred and no seeded-defect repair is claimed.
